source.title: Continuous Variation of Cauchy Data Spaces. Task - Results - Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For a smooth compact Riemannian manifold M with boundary Σ, Hermitian vector bundles E and F over M, and a general linear first-order elliptic differential operator A: C∞(M, E) → C∞(M, F), determine to what extent the structural properties known for Dirac-type operators continue to hold without assuming the Dirac or near-boundary product-form setting with fixed geometric data. In particular, after rewriting A near the boundary in product form A = J(x)(∂x + B(x)) plus lower-order terms, ask how far one can recover, for such arbitrary first-order elliptic operators, the same package of results emphasized for Dirac-type operators: a transparent and canonical Calderón projection, the Lagrangian property of the Cauchy data space, self-adjoint Fredholm extensions under regular pseudodifferential boundary conditions, the Cobordism Theorem, and continuous dependence of the associated data under variation of the operator, domain, and boundary geometry.
accepted.context_brief: Generalization of Dirac-type boundary-value theory to arbitrary first-order elliptic operators.

evidence.quote: In our joint papers, we wanted to transgress the limitations of the general functional-analytical approach: we don’t wish to keep the domain fixed under variation; nor to restrict to bounded (i.e., 0 order) perturbations; nor to confine the applicability to ordinary differential equations or Dirac type operators with constant coefficients in normal direction (product case) close to boundary.

We took up the challenge of general linear elliptic differential operators; investigated weak inner UCP; established the existence of self-adjoint Fredholm extensions; admitted variation of domain and skew boundaries, and investigated uniform structures and continuous perturbations.
We ask How special are operators of Dirac type compared to arbitrary linear first order elliptic differential operators?

From that alone, we emphasize, one can derive the transparent definition of the Calderón projection, the Lagrangian property of the Cauchy data space, the existence of a self-adjoint Fredholm extension given by a regular pseudodiffernetial boundary condition, the Cobordism Theorem, and the continuous dependence of input data.
